question: Did miracles continue after the apostles?

answers.label: Yes: exorcisms, healings and other wonders went on
The great signs ended with the apostolic age

overview.text: Second-century apologists claimed present miracles as evidence: exorcism in Jesus' name (Justin), healings and even raisings from the dead (Irenaeus), and a public test of demons before Roman judges (Tertullian).
By the late fourth century, some said the great signs had ceased, as Chrysostom did of tongues. Augustine first agreed, then recorded many miracles at the martyrs' shrines (City of God 22.8).

quotes.author: Justin Martyr
quotes.english: And now we who believe in Jesus our Lord, crucified under Pontius Pilate, exorcise all demons and evil spirits, and have them subject to us.
quotes.original: Καὶ νῦν ἡμεῖς, οἱ πιστεύοντες ἐπὶ τὸν σταυρωθέντα ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου Ἰησοῦν κύριον ἡμῶν, τὰ δαιμόνια πάντα καὶ πνεύματα πονηρὰ ἐξορκίζοντες ὑποτασσόμενα ἡμῖν ἔχομεν.
quotes.context: Exorcism in the name of Jesus was the most common claim of present miracles.

quotes.author: Irenaeus of Lyons (quoted by Eusebius)
quotes.work: Against Heresies 2.32.4 and 5.6.1, in Eusebius, Church History
quotes.english: Some drive out demons truly and certainly ... others heal the sick by laying on of hands and make them well. And already, as we said, even the dead have been raised and remained with us many years.
quotes.original: οἶ μὲν γὰρ δαίμονας ἐλαύνουσι βεβαίως καὶ ἀληθῶς ... ἄλλοι δὲ τοὺς κάμνοντας δια τῆς τῶν χειρῶν ἐπιθέσεως ἰῶνται καὶ ὑγιεῖς ἀποκαθιστᾶσιν. ἤδη δὲ, καθὼς ἔφαμεν, καὶ νεκροὶ ἠγέρθησαν, καὶ παρέμειναν σὺν ἡμῖν ἔτεσιν ἱκανοῖς.
quotes.context: Irenaeus claims raisings from the dead in his own time.

quotes.author: Tertullian
quotes.english: Let someone be brought before your tribunals who is plainly possessed by a demon. Ordered by any Christian to speak, that spirit will confess itself a demon as truly as elsewhere it falsely calls itself a god. ... Unless they confess themselves demons, not daring to lie to a Christian, then shed that impudent Christian's blood on the spot!
quotes.original: Edatur hic aliqui ibidem sub tribunalibus vestris, quem daemone agi constet; iussus a quolibet Christiano loqui spiritus ille tam se daemonem confitebitur de vero quam alibi deum de falso. ... nisi se daemones confessi fuerint, Christiano mentiri non au
quotes.context: Tertullian offers a public test before Roman judges.

quotes.author: Gregory of Nyssa
quotes.english: For immediately, not long after, the staff, rooted into the banks, became a tree. ... Such was the power of Gregory the Great, or rather of God working the wonders in him.
quotes.original: Εὐθὺς γὰρ οὐ μετὰ πολὺν χρόνον ἡ μὲν βακτηρία, ταῖς ὄχθαις ἐῤῥιζωθεῖσα, δένδρον ἐγένετο. ... Τοιαύτη τοῦ μεγάλου Γρηγορίου ἡ δύναμις, μᾶλλον δὲ τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ ἐνεργοῦντος ἐν ἐκείνῳ τὰ θαύματα.
quotes.context: Gregory the Wonderworker (c. 213 to c. 270), bishop of Neocaesarea a century after the apostles, prays at the flooding river Lycus and plants his staff on the bank; it grows into a tree which, Gregory of Nyssa says, still turns the river back in flood. The Life presents his wonders, the dried lake, the moved rock and this river among them, as God's power working in a post-apostolic bishop.

quotes.author: John Chrysostom
quotes.english: This whole passage is very obscure. The obscurity comes from our ignorance of the facts and from their absence, since they used to happen then but do not happen now. And why do they not happen now? ... Why did they happen then and no longer now? Let us put that off to another time. ... What then happened then? Whoever was baptized at once spoke in tongues.
quotes.original: Τοῦτο ἅπαν τὸ χωρίον σφόδρα ἐστὶν ἀσαφές· τὴν δὲ ἀσάφειαν ἡ τῶν πραγμάτων ἄγνοιά τε καὶ ἔλλειψις ποιεῖ τῶν τότε μὲν συμβαινόντων, νῦν δὲ οὐ γινομένων. Καὶ τίνος ἕνεκεν οὐ γίνεται νῦν; ... Τί δήποτε γὰρ τότε μὲν ἐγίνετο, νῦν δὲ οὐκέτι; Ἀλλὰ τοῦτο μὲν εἰς αὖθις ἀναβαλλώμεθα, τέως δὲ τὰ συμβαίνοντα τότε λέγωμεν. Τί οὖν τότε συνέβαινεν; Εἴ τις ἐβαπτίσατο, γλώσσαις εὐθέως ἐλάλει
quotes.context: Chrysostom elsewhere explains that miracles were needed at the beginning, to plant the faith, and are less needed now.

gaps.author: Augustine of Hippo
gaps.why: His change of mind on present miracles.

gaps.author: Athanasius
gaps.why: Healings and exorcisms of the first monk.
